Borrowed items are due on the date printed on the visitor's receipt.
The quiet study room is available when no event is scheduled.
Visitors can suggest titles on a paper request form at the front desk.
Schedule changes are posted at the front desk and on the library website.
Reading groups meet once each month in the community room.

scenarios.title: Local history museum
notes: The local history museum is closed on Mondays and open from ten to five on other days.
The harbor gallery contains maps, photographs, and recorded interviews.
A guided harbor-gallery tour starts at eleven thirty on Saturdays.
Visitors may take notes but should not use flash photography near original photographs.
The research desk accepts appointment requests by email at least two days ahead.
Admission is free for children under twelve when accompanied by an adult.

scenarios.title: Community garden
notes: The community garden has twelve raised beds shared by neighborhood members.
Members water the beds early in the morning on Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday.
The west-side rain barrel is reserved for seedlings during dry weather.
Compost is collected in the covered bin beside the tool shed.
The tool shed is unlocked by the rotating volunteer whose name is on the weekly board.
The monthly work party begins at nine on the first Sunday.

scenarios.title: Neighborhood repair workshop
notes: The neighborhood repair workshop accepts small household appliances, bicycles, and clothing for repair sessions.
Open repair hours are Wednesday evenings from six to eight and Saturday mornings from nine to noon.
A visitor should bring any replacement part they already own and the appliance's power cable.
The workshop cannot accept gas appliances, devices with swollen batteries, or items that are wet.
Bicycle repairs are handled at the outdoor bench; clothing repairs are handled in the sewing room.
Volunteers inspect an item first and explain any safety concern before beginning work.
The workshop asks visitors to book a slot online because walk-in capacity is limited.
A booking confirmation lists the assigned volunteer and the expected session length.
Basic hand tools are available, but specialty parts and materials are not included.
Visitors under sixteen must attend with an adult during all repair sessions.
The workshop entrance is on Cedar Street beside the community center loading bay.
A repair that cannot be completed during the visit may be continued at the next open session.

scenarios.title: Coastal weather station field guide
notes: The coastal weather station records air temperature, rainfall, wind direction, and tide level.
A volunteer reads the manual rain gauge at seven each morning and records the result in millimeters.
The anemometer is mounted on the north mast, while the wind vane is mounted above the instrument shed.
Wind direction is reported as a compass heading averaged over a ten-minute observation period.
The tide staff is fixed to the east pier and is read against the local chart datum.
Storm observations are taken from inside the instrument shed; volunteers must not climb the mast during high winds.
The thermometer screen is shaded and ventilated so direct sunlight does not warm the sensor.
Rain-gauge readings are marked invalid if leaves, salt spray, or ice obstruct the funnel.
The data notebook records the observer's initials and the exact local observation time.
If a sensor appears damaged, the volunteer logs the issue and contacts the station coordinator.
The station's monthly summary reports the highest wind speed and total rainfall.
A backup battery is stored in the dry cabinet and is checked on the first day of each month.
